headline: Engram: AI sampler turns AI hallucinations into experimental music
summary: Thoughtful Things' new instrument uses a custom "tiny AI" to mangle audio and create uncanny sounds, running entirely offline.
details: Music startup Thoughtful Things has launched Engram, a sampler and groovebox designed to explore the creative potential of AI audio models.
Unlike AI music generators focused on pop hits, Engram is built for experimental sound design, using a custom-trained "tiny AI" that runs locally without an internet connection.
The device can mangle incoming audio and even hallucinate entirely new sounds, with founder Evan King describing it as a "field recorder for latent space."
Engram draws inspiration from circuit bending, allowing users to tweak and even "break" its AI models for unique sonic textures.
Thoughtful Things emphasizes ethical AI training, stating that Engram's models are trained only on audio licensed for commercial use.
The company also plans to release Engram's firmware, enabling users to customize it or load their own AI models.
Engram is currently available for pre-order on Kickstarter starting at $675, with an estimated retail price between $850 and $900.
caption:
This new AI sampler doesn't just make music—it explores AI hallucinations for experimental sound design.

Music startup Thoughtful Things has launched Engram, a sampler and groovebox designed to explore the creative potential of AI audio models.

Unlike AI music generators focused on pop hits, Engram is built for experimental sound design, using a custom-trained "tiny AI" that runs locally without an internet connection.

The device can mangle incoming audio and even hallucinate entirely new sounds, with founder Evan King describing it as a "field recorder for latent space."

Engram draws inspiration from circuit bending, allowing users to tweak and even "break" its AI models for unique sonic textures.

Thoughtful Things emphasizes ethical AI training, stating that Engram's models are trained only on audio licensed for commercial use.

The company also plans to release Engram's firmware, enabling users to customize it or load their own AI models.

Engram is currently available for pre-order on Kickstarter starting at $675, with an estimated retail price between $850 and $900.

#AI #MusicTech #ExperimentalMusic #SoundDesign #ThoughtfulThings

Source: The Verge

headline_marked: Anthropic CEO [[Dario Amodei to dine with Trump]] amid AI safety debate
headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to dine with Trump amid AI safety debate
summary: Amodei, who advocates for cautious AI development, is set to meet with former President Donald Trump at the White House.
details: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is scheduled for a private dinner with former President Donald Trump at the White House, marking their first one-on-one meeting.
The meeting comes as Amodei and Trump have publicly diverged on the approach to AI safety, with Amodei calling for caution and Trump dismissing AI concerns as a "hoax."
This dinner follows a recent period of scrutiny for Anthropic, including a Pentagon designation as a supply-chain risk due to its efforts to implement safety guardrails on its AI technology.
